findings.reason: The protected source compresses iteration, a two-part segment-start condition, Boolean-to-integer conversion, and accumulation into one sum expression. Although correct, that packed formulation hides the single transition being counted. The candidate makes the scan, condition, increment, and return explicit in six direct lines.

The protected generator uses the prohibited generic name index. The candidate uses conventional i and c for a position and character, plus segments for the genuine algorithmic result being accumulated.

The inert candidate is the conventional interview solution: scan once and increment exactly when a non-space character either begins the string or follows a space. Its boundary condition is visible at the point of use, and it preserves O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space without materializing substrings.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 434 and its Python string-to-integer surface. The app contract matches the native countSegments parameter and result. The modular Reference preserves the contiguous non-space definition, both current source examples, the first explanation's five exact pieces, and all three character-domain constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064806234 and is expression-for-expression aligned with the protected app source apart from its Solution wrapper. The candidate preserves the identical transition predicate and linear data flow while expanding the proposed control flow and names; neither protected source nor the verified manifest changed.

The 16-, 64-, and 256-character single-segment tiers span 16x within the source limit and force a backward-rescanning alternative onto its quadratic path. The candidate passed all 11 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.74x the reference runtime. A correct quadratic backward-scan control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 81.34x.

The candidate-targeted Approach exactly identifies segment-start transitions, uses i, c, and segments as the candidate does, proves the one-to-one correspondence with maximal runs, states O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space, and distinguishes spaces from all allowed punctuation.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves the short problem definition, both example facts in order, the first example's explanation and exact segment list, every constraint, and the literal ASCII space rule. The statement contains no images, tables, diagrams, notes, or follow-up.
